info.title: FoPost API
info.description:
REST API for FoPost — schedule, publish, and analyze social media content across every connected platform.

## Authentication

Programmatic access uses an API key sent in the `X-API-Key` header. Keys are created in the FoPost dashboard under **Settings → API Keys** and are limited to the scopes granted at creation. Requests from the FoPost dashboard use a JWT bearer token instead (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`), which implicitly carries all scopes. Either method works on every endpoint in this document unless noted otherwise.

## Scopes

Each operation lists its required scope (also machine-readable as `x-fopost-scope`): `posts` (includes publishing, deliveries, and media), `workspaces`, `accounts`, `labels`, `webhooks`, `analytics`, `automations`.

## Errors

Errors return `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<explanation>" }` with a matching HTTP status. Some errors include additional context fields.

## Rate limiting

Requests are rate limited per API key, per minute, with a ceiling set by the plan behind the key. Every response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; exceeding the limit returns `429` with error code `too_many_requests`, a `retry_after` field and a `Retry-After` header. Mutating endpoints additionally require an active subscription and return `403` with error code `subscription_required` without one.

## Pagination

List endpoints that paginate accept `page` and `per_page` query parameters and return a `meta` object with `current_page`, `per_page`, `total`, and `last_page`.

get.description: Returns the OpenAPI 3.1 description of the FoPost public API. No auth required.
RFC 8414 discovery document: endpoint URLs, supported grant types, PKCE methods and scopes. No auth required.

302.description: Redirect to the consent screen, or to redirect_uri with an error

get.description: Send the user here in a browser. After validating the client and redirect_uri the user signs in, picks a workspace and approves the scopes; the browser is then sent to `redirect_uri` with `code` and `state`, or with `error=access_denied`. PKCE with S256 is required. Errors about the client or redirect_uri answer 400 here instead of redirecting.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Exactly one of the URIs registered for the client

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Space-separated scopes, the same names as API-key scopes

post.summary: Exchange a code or refresh token

400.description: invalid_grant (wrong verifier, used or expired code), invalid_scope, unsupported_grant_type

post.description: `grant_type=authorization_code` takes `code`, `redirect_uri`, `code_verifier` and `client_id`; `grant_type=refresh_token` takes `refresh_token` and `client_id`. A confidential client also sends `client_secret` (or HTTP Basic). Refresh tokens rotate on every use. Access tokens last one hour and go in `Authorization: Bearer`; they carry the approved scopes and are confined to the approved workspace.
RFC 7009. Revokes the grant behind an access or refresh token; answers 200 whether or not the token existed. Requires `client_id` (and `client_secret` for a confidential client).

client_secret.description: Only for a confidential client; shown once

post.description:
RFC 7591 registration for signed-in developers: use your API key. The client is owned by your account. `client_uri` is your site; every redirect URI must be https on that host or a subdomain of it (loopback http is allowed for native and local clients) and is matched exactly. The client name may not use the product name. `token_endpoint_auth_method` defaults to `none` (a public client, PKCE only); `client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post` issues a secret that is shown once.

MCP clients may register without a credential when every redirect URI is loopback or on a supported MCP client host; `client_uri` is then optional and the client has no owner.

Requires the `workspaces` scope when using an API key.

get.description:

parameters.description: Pass `oldest` for ascending order; default is newest first

post.description:
Creates a draft or scheduled post targeting one or more connected accounts. Content is an ordered list of blocks (threads use multiple blocks).

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

get.description: Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

409.description: Post cannot be updated: it is publishing or cancelled, a published post was given accounts or a schedule, or one of its networks cannot edit a live post (`unsupported_platforms` lists them)

put.description:
Arrays (`content`, `accounts`, `labels`, `settings`) are replaced wholesale when provided. A draft, scheduled or pending-approval post takes any change. A published post takes a content change only (`content`, `title`, `settings`, `labels`, `internal_title`, `summary`), and only when every network it is live on can edit in place (see `remote_edit` on the post accounts); the change is then pushed to each network and reported in `remote_edits`. Reaching a network needs the `publish` scope as well. A published post on a network that cannot edit answers 409 with `unsupported_platforms`.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the post. Already-published platform posts stay up unless `remove_from_platform` is set, which also asks each network that supports it (see `remote_delete` on the post accounts) to take the post down. Reaching a network needs the `publish` scope as well.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

parameters.name: remove_from_platform
parameters.description: Also delete the published post from the networks that support it

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

409.description: Post is not in a draft or scheduled state

422.description: Invalid post id, or all target accounts have expired/revoked credentials (`health_check_failed`)

post.description:
Queues delivery of a draft or scheduled post to its assigned accounts (or the `accountIds` subset). Accounts with expired or revoked credentials are failed immediately; degraded accounts publish with a warning. Delivery is asynchronous — poll the deliveries endpoint or subscribe to webhooks for the outcome. With `options.dryRun` the request validates and returns the target accounts without publishing (200 instead of 202).

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

409.description: Post state does not allow retrying

422.description: Invalid post id, or every selected delivery exceeded the retry limit (`retry_limit_exceeded`)

post.description:
Re-queues failed deliveries of a failed, partially failed, or published post. Resending to already-published accounts requires `includePublished: true`. Deliveries past the retry limit are reported in `exceeded` and skipped.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

Cancels pending, queued, or delayed deliveries (optionally limited to `accountIds`) and recalculates the post status. Send `{}` to cancel all.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

post.summary: Take a published post down everywhere

409.description: Post is not published, or a network cannot delete a live post

post.description:
Deletes the post on every network it is live on and marks each delivery `unpublished`; the post stays as a record. Refused as a whole with 409 and `unsupported_platforms` when one of those networks cannot delete a live post (see `remote_delete` on the post accounts). A network that refuses at the time keeps its delivery published and answers `removed: false`.

Requires the `publish` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

Checks each assigned account for hard blockers (`issues`) and returns advisory per-platform content quality signals. Signals never block publishing.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

post.summary: Validate content for a set of platforms
post.description:

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

post.summary: Check text length against platform limits
post.description:
Counts the text the way each platform does (some bill every link at a flat rate, some count bytes) and compares it with the platform limit.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

post.summary: Check a media file by URL
post.description:
Fetches the file and runs the upload checks on it: allowed type, bytes that match the declared type, and the size ceiling. The file is not stored. A URL that cannot be fetched, including one that points at a private address, is a `400`.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

get.description:

get.summary: List publish runs for a post

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

post.description:
Copies the post — content, target accounts, per-platform settings and labels — into a new draft in the same workspace. Schedule, approval and delivery state are not carried over.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

get.description:

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

post.summary: Bulk reschedule, relabel or delete posts
post.description:
Applies one action to up to 200 posts in a single transaction. Every post is validated first: any id outside the workspace answers 404 and any post that is no longer draft or scheduled answers 409, in both cases without changing anything. `shift` moves each `schedule_at` by `offset_minutes` (negative moves earlier) and refuses offsets that land in the past; `label` applies `label_ids` with mode `replace` (an empty list clears), `add` or `remove`; `delete` soft-deletes the posts and cancels their queued deliveries.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

Dry-runs a CSV/TSV import (max 500 data rows, 2 MB) and returns per-row validation results without creating anything. Columns: `content` (required), `schedule_at` (ISO 8601 or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` in the workspace timezone), `accounts` (comma-separated account ids or platform names), `labels`, `media_url`, and per-platform overrides `caption_<platform>`.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

Re-validates the uploaded CSV/TSV and creates one scheduled post per row, all stamped with a fresh batch id. All-or-nothing: if any row fails validation, nothing is created and the failing rows are returned.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

delete.description:
Soft-deletes the batch's posts that are still draft or scheduled and cancels their queued deliveries. Refused with 409 if any post in the batch has already published or is publishing.

Requires the `posts` scope when using an API key.

Requires an active subscription; without one the request fails with 403 `subscription_required`.

The account is tagged with `externalUserId`. `redirectUrl` must be on a domain in the workspace redirect allowlist (dashboard → API Keys); the user is sent there with `status`, `platform`, `account_id` and `external_user_id` once connected. `workspaceId` may be omitted for a key bound to one workspace.

Poll `GET /v1/accounts/telegram/connect-code/status` for the outcome. `workspaceId` may be omitted for a key bound to one workspace.

Requires the `accounts` scope when using an API key.

The account leaves its account groups.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: API key created in the FoPost dashboard. A key may be bound to a single workspace, in which case every request is confined to it: naming any other workspace returns 403, and listings return only that workspace. Keys created without a workspace keep access to every workspace on the account.

BearerAuth.description: Session token used by the FoPost dashboard

OAuth2.description: For third-party apps acting on behalf of a FoPost user. Authorization code with PKCE (S256) is required. The token is confined to the workspace the user approved and to the scopes they granted.

headers.description: Custom headers sent with every delivery. Values are write-only and never returned; signing headers cannot be overridden.

secret.description: Rotates the signing secret; the new value is returned once in this response.

headers.description: Replaces the header set. A null value keeps the stored value of an existing header; a top-level null clears every header.
